metadata.note: The Schenectady and Duanesburgh Railroad -- 14.2 miles from Schenectady southwest to Delanson, in the town of Duanesburg, joining the Delaware and Hudson's Saratoga lines at one end to the Albany and Susquehanna at the other. It was chartered as the Schenectady and Susquehanna Railroad on Dec 27 1869 and opened about August 1872, but lasted under that name less than a year: the property was sold under foreclosure on July 10 1873 and conveyed two days later to the Schenectady and Duanesburgh Railroad, which was incorporated that July. It was leased to the Delaware and Hudson Canal Company from first to last and never ran as an independent railroad, being merged into the Delaware and Hudson Company outright on Aug 4 1903. It fills a gap the Albany and Susquehanna layer explicitly leaves: that file's notes list the Schenectady and Susquehanna among the branches off its corridor that it does not draw. The corridor is still in freight service today, but freight-only years are not drawn (CLAUDE.md Rule 1): the map ends the line in 1963.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schenectady_and_Duanesburgh_Railroad (incorporated Dec 27 1869 as the Schenectady and Susquehanna Railroad; opened about August 1872; always leased to the Delaware and Hudson Canal Company; owned the 14.2-mile / 22.9 km line between the Saratoga and Schenectady Railroad at Schenectady and the Albany and Susquehanna Railroad at Delanson, New York; the property was sold under foreclosure July 10 1873 and conveyed to the Schenectady and Duanesburgh Railroad July 12, that company being incorporated in July 1873; merged into the Delaware and Hudson Company Aug 4 1903).

https://www.schenectadyhistory.org/railroads/index.html and https://www.schenectadyhistory.org/resources/mvgw/history/087.html (Schenectady railroad history: the Schenectady & Duanesburgh was started in 1869 and completed in 1873; the branch runs south to Quaker Street and there connects with the Albany & Susquehanna, now the Delaware & Hudson).

data/albany_and_susquehanna_railroad.geojson in this repository, whose metadata names the Schenectady and Susquehanna as one of the branches off the A&S corridor that it does not draw -- this layer supplies it.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: All frequencies and speeds are estimates. The intermediate stations between Schenectady and Delanson were not found, so the route is drawn from the two endpoints and the corridor between them rather than station by station. Sources differ slightly on the completion date -- Wikipedia gives an opening of about August 1872 under the Schenectady and Susquehanna name, while the Schenectady history pages say the Schenectady & Duanesburgh was 'started in 1869 and completed in 1873', which appears to date the reorganisation rather than the track. Ownership after the 1903 D&H merger, and the identity of the present-day operator, are not sourced. The end year is the weakest date in this file: when passenger trains last ran Schenectady-Delanson is unknown. 1963 is used because that is when D&H passenger service ended on the Susquehanna Division as a whole (trains 250 and 208, Jan 24 1963), but this branch was the D&H's through freight route around Albany and its own passenger service plausibly ended decades earlier. A D&H public timetable or Official Guide listing for the branch would settle it.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API, shortest-path search over the OSM rail graph within a narrow corridor bounding box between Schenectady and Delanson. A first attempt padded the search area widely enough to pull in the Selkirk and Hudson Line tangle around Schenectady and the router wandered, giving a 27 km result against a booked 22.9; restricting the graph to the corridor fixed it.

Result: traced 23.53 km on real track against the company's booked 14.2 miles (22.85 km), a 1.03x match, with endpoint snaps of 220 m at Schenectady and 111 m at Delanson. No straight-line approximations. The corridor is still active freight track, which is why it traces cleanly.
Per-leg tracing result: Schenectady -> Delanson: 40 pts, 23.53km vs 22.85km booked (1.03x), snap 220/111m [rail]
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-08-26: the 1903-2026 segment was cut back to 1903-1963. Its own note said the corridor "remains in freight service today" as the Carman Subdivision / NS D&H South Line, so the drawn years were asserting passenger service through six decades of freight-only operation. 1963 is the documented end of D&H passenger service on the Susquehanna Division (trains 250 and 208, Jan 24 1963); the branch's own last passenger train remains unsourced and is recorded in not_yet_sourced. See CLAUDE.md Rule 1.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Merged into the Delaware and Hudson Company Aug 4 1903, ending the separate corporate existence. Drawn to 1963 as the outside bound of passenger service in this corridor: D&H Susquehanna Division passenger service ended when trains 250 and 208, the last Albany-Binghamton round trip, were discontinued Jan 24 1963 (see albany_and_susquehanna_railroad.geojson). The Schenectady branch's own last passenger train is NOT sourced and may well have come off decades earlier -- this branch was primarily the D&H's through freight route around Albany, not a passenger main -- so treat the later years here as an upper bound, not a claim of service. The rails are still there and still busy, but with freight only: OpenStreetMap carries the corridor as the Carman Subdivision, the NS D&H South Line and the Delanson siding. That freight era is deliberately not drawn (CLAUDE.md Rule 1). Frequency estimated, unsourced
sources: Segment-level (end year only): the 1963 end is taken from the documented end of D&H passenger service in this corridor -- trains 250 and 208, the last Albany-Binghamton round trip, discontinued Jan 24 1963.
